tasks.short: Audit the actual solar installation site

steps.what: Inspect the site, measure roof geometry, assess access and shading, and examine structural and electrical conditions within the engineer's competence.
Capture actual measurements, photograph references and inaccessible areas in the site audit notes; distinguish observed conditions from drawings and assumptions.

Assemble the site audit report in {DOCS}; configure its native form and photo captions to reuse the captured fields, then check every observation, limitation, unit and photograph against the site notes.
Save the checked final site audit report to the project record in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure the site audit form and report template in {DOCS} before considering a separate application. The engineer records the actual site evidence and the template assembles the report; physical inspection and interpretation remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unlabelled photographs and inconsistent measurement headings made report assembly repetitive.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields and reusable report sections can preserve measurement and photograph references.
tasks.still_hard: Concealed structure, inaccessible electrical equipment and uncertain drawings require further investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a site observation is insufficient to support a safe design.

ambition.what: No new decision right; the engineer still owns the site audit.

tasks.altitude: Less report layout work; the same site inspection and limits of competence apply.

evidence.claim: Document forms can reuse captured fields and photograph captions without interpreting structural conditions.

assumptions: Boundary is the engineer's site audit through its stored report, not later design, specialist inspections or customer distribution. Shares are a scenario, not a measured baseline.

The engineer produces site ID, inspection date, location, dimension, unit, measurement method, photo ID, observation and access limitation during s1-s2. Missing fields stay explicitly unknown; manual notes and labelled photographs are the fallback, with their capture time retained.
Native form and template configuration is tried first. Savings apply only where the same report currently requires manual assembly; no inspection or source capture is removed.
The ordinary author check in s3 approves the final report for s4; an edit invalidates approval. No extra approval meeting is added.
unknowns: Current audit form and report assembly time
Availability and reliability of existing drawings
research_questions: Can the native document form retain photo and location references offline?

already_counted.description: Check the assembled report against the actual audit evidence and limitations.

incremental.description: Maintain report fields and test photo-reference reuse.

approvals.approved_version: Final audit report snapshot checked at the end of s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Manual report assembly scenario: 19 hours reduced by 30% gives 5.7 gross hours, less 1 upkeep hour. Zero where the native template is already configured; inspection and note capture remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan solar development, monitoring and evaluation

steps.what: Read the solar project scope, site audit, connection constraints and monitoring requirements; resolve missing inputs with their owners.
Choose development stages, evaluation questions, monitoring points and acceptance evidence, and agree realistic dependencies with the people doing the work.
Build the activity network and monitoring schedule in {PROJECT}; use native dependencies, recurring activities and plan views to calculate dates and assemble the selected work packages.
Review the completed plan for feasible access windows, installation sequence, commissioning evidence, sensor availability and evaluation responsibilities; correct and approve its final version.
Commit the checked final solar project plan as the current project baseline in {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Use native planning features in {PROJECT} for the engineer's chosen activities and dependencies. Dates and views update deterministically; engineering acceptance criteria, resource agreements and the final plan remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates and monitoring activities were maintained separately from the dependency network.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning systems can calculate schedules from explicit durations, calendars and dependencies.
tasks.still_hard: A schedule cannot decide whether the proposed evidence will demonstrate adequate solar system performance.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible evaluation criteria and negotiate a feasible sequence.

ambition.what: Compare the schedule effect of a changed commissioning date before agreeing it.

tasks.altitude: The engineer can test scheduling alternatives during planning without gaining authority over other teams' capacity.

reach.task: Link drawing delivery dates to installation activities

evidence.claim: Native project scheduling can recalculate explicit activity dependencies and calendars.

assumptions: Boundary is plan preparation and baseline storage. Actual installation, monitoring readings and evaluation are downstream tasks. Shares describe an adoption scenario.

The engineer captures activity ID, owner, duration, dependency, access window, calendar, monitoring point, evaluation criterion and evidence reference in s2-s3. Owners confirm constraints in existing planning discussions; no free collection service is assumed. Missing values are resolved manually, not inferred.
Try native schedule configuration first. Only date propagation and repeated plan assembly lose time. Other participants' labour remains outside the focal denominator and is unchanged.
The completed and corrected plan exists before s4 approves the s5 baseline. Further changes require the same ordinary plan review.
unknowns: Reliability of resource and access commitments
research_questions: Can native baseline views preserve monitoring criteria alongside the schedule?

already_counted.description: Review schedule construction and its input fields.

incremental.description: Maintain calendar, activity and monitoring templates.

approvals.approved_version: Completed plan baseline snapshot checked at the end of s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native scheduling replaces 35% of the 30-hour schedule construction share: 10.5 gross hours less 2 upkeep hours. Zero if these functions are already used; scope, negotiation and final review stay intact.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design building solar power or thermal systems

steps.what: Verify the building loads, site audit, usable area, shading, service interfaces and applicable design requirements for the chosen solar project.
Lay out collectors or modules and their components in the solar design software {OTHER}; use native geometry reuse and component libraries while selecting spacing, access and interfaces manually.

Evaluate the candidate layout using native solar design calculations in {OTHER}: electrical ratings and string limits for PV, or collector, storage and hydraulic operating cases for solar thermal; inspect all inputs, units and boundary conditions.
Resolve structural, electrical or thermal interfaces with the relevant specialists and complete the design record; check the final layout, components, calculations and limitations together.
Save the checked final solar system design to the controlled project record in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure component libraries, geometry reuse and operating-case calculations in the existing solar design software {OTHER}. The engineer selects the design, checks the physics and coordinates interfaces; {DOCS} stores the final checked revision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated geometry entry and calculation setup were separate from the selected component specifications.
tasks.enabler_now: Native design libraries and parametric calculations can reuse explicit geometry and ratings.
tasks.still_hard: Roof load paths, unusual shading and operating extremes need engineering judgement and specialist evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether a calculated alternative is buildable and safe for this building.

ambition.what: Compare a second feasible collector or module layout before fixing the design.

tasks.altitude: More time for interface and operating-envelope checks; no new construction approval rights.

reach.learn: Design revision references and component identification.

evidence.claim: Solar engineering software can reuse component ratings, geometry and deterministic operating-case calculations.

assumptions: One PV or solar thermal design instance is modelled, not both as duplicated work. Boundary ends at the stored design; procurement, permit submission and installation release are separate. Shares are illustrative.

The engineer verifies building ID, roof geometry, orientation, shading observations, load series with units, weather source, component revision and ratings, and interface constraints in s1-s3. Existing site audit and specification producers supply source files; manual entry and source checking remain counted. Missing structural evidence is obtained from specialists, never guessed.

Test native design functions before custom code. Gains are repeated geometry and arithmetic setup only, not solver runtime, specialist labour or design judgement. s4 includes existing interface discussions and final record writing.
The author check covers the final saved design revision. Changes after s4 invalidate its approval; storage does not authorise construction.
unknowns: Existing solar design package features and current use
Availability of verified load and structural data
research_questions: Do native libraries preserve component revision and unit provenance through calculation exports?

already_counted.description: Review operating cases, input units and calculation applicability.

incremental.description: Validate component library changes and calculation templates.

approvals.approved_version: Final layout, component list and calculation revision checked at the end of s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Layout setup saves 5 hours and operating-case setup 8.75 per 100 baseline hours; 2 upkeep hours leave 11.75 net. Zero if native reuse is already established. Full interface and final engineering review remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Support solar installation and commissioning teams

steps.what: Read the installation question, current design revision and actual test or monitoring evidence, and inspect the relevant site condition where needed.
Give technical direction and explain test findings to the installation team; resolve uncertainty through the normal engineering and commissioning responsibilities.
Write the actual guidance and follow-up in the existing {PROJECT} issue; configure native design-reference and test-reference fields, then check the final note against what was actually advised.
Post the checked final guidance note to the existing {PROJECT} issue for the installation team.

tasks.design: Reuse the existing {PROJECT} issue's native design and test reference fields when recording guidance. Inspection, explanation and commissioning judgement remain with the engineer; only repeated note headings and references change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance notes repeatedly retyped the design and test references already attached to the issue.
tasks.enabler_now: Native issue fields can retain those references alongside the engineer's actual guidance.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected wiring, hydraulic behaviour or commissioning results cannot be resolved from a template.
tasks.human_edge: Explain a safe course of action to the people at the equipment and recognise when work must pause.
tasks.altitude: The engineer keeps the same installation support duties with a small reduction in repeated references.

reach.learn: Separate observed results from proposed remedies.

evidence.claim: Native issue fields can reuse existing design and test references without generating technical advice.

assumptions: Boundary is the engineer's support through its existing guidance note, not the installation team's physical work or a separate system release. No new reporting duty is introduced. Shares are an illustrative case with a current issue note.

The engineer captures issue ID, actual observation, test reference, design revision, guidance and follow-up owner in s1-s3. The installer produces actual test evidence in existing work; the engineer reads and verifies it here. Missing references are entered manually. Planned tests never count as completed.
Native issue configuration comes first. Only repeated headings and existing references are reused; actual advice and evidence capture retain their effort.
s3's ordinary author check binds the final posted note and audience. An edit voids approval. A design change or energisation requires its separate authorised process, not this note.
unknowns: Whether current issue notes already retain design references
Actual proportion of support done without any written note
research_questions: Can the existing issue preserve the precise design revision alongside the guidance?

already_counted.description: Write and check the actual technical guidance note.

approvals.approved_version: Final guidance note and issue audience checked at the end of s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Reusing references removes 10% of the existing 14-hour note share: 1.4 gross hours less 0.4 upkeep. Zero for already-configured issues or entirely spoken support. Posting and technical work retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Solar engineers retain site, design and commissioning judgement while reusing verified inputs in native planning and design tools.
reach: Coordinate traceable site measurements with surveyors
Align design revisions with electrical and electronics drafters
role.ambitious_version: Compare feasible solar alternatives with traceable site evidence before committing the design.
